description: The “fill of blood” associated with the Massagetae queen Tomyris comes from Herodotus’ account of her defeat of Cyrus the Great. After Cyrus was killed in battle, Tomyris reportedly had his head placed in a vessel or skin filled with human blood, declaring that although he had destroyed her son through treachery and thirsted for blood, she would now give him his fill. Whether literally historical or a dramatic literary tradition, the episode became the defining symbol of Tomyris’ vengeance, portraying her as a formidable ruler who defeated one of antiquity’s greatest conquerors.
